View information about a GitHub Release.

Without an explicit tag name argument, the latest release in the project
is shown.

For more information about output formatting flags, see `gh help formatting`.

USAGE
  gh release view [<tag>] [flags]

FLAGS
  -q, --jq expression     Filter JSON output using a jq expression
      --json fields       Output JSON with the specified fields
  -t, --template string   Format JSON output using a Go template; see "gh help formatting"
  -w, --web               Open the release in the browser

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

JSON FIELDS
  apiUrl, assets, author, body, createdAt, databaseId, id, isDraft, isImmutable,
  isPrerelease, name, publishedAt, tagName, tarballUrl, targetCommitish,
  uploadUrl, url, zipballUrl

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`

Download assets from a GitHub release.

Without an explicit tag name argument, assets are downloaded from the
latest release in the project. In this case, `--pattern` or `--archive`
is required.


USAGE
  gh release download [<tag>] [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-escape-sequences   Allow printing terminal escape sequences when writing an asset to standard output
  -A, --archive format           Download the source code archive in the specified format (zip or tar.gz)
      --clobber                  Overwrite existing files of the same name
  -D, --dir directory            The directory to download files into (default ".")
  -O, --output file              The file to write a single asset to (use "-" to write to standard output)
  -p, --pattern stringArray      Download only assets that match a glob pattern
      --skip-existing            Skip downloading when files of the same name exist

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Download all assets from a specific release
  $ gh release download v1.2.3
  
  # Download only Debian packages for the latest release
  $ gh release download --pattern '*.deb'
  
  # Specify multiple file patterns
  $ gh release download -p '*.deb' -p '*.rpm'
  
  # Download the archive of the source code for a release
  $ gh release download v1.2.3 --archive=zip

  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual

commands.stdout:
rup: the command line of roundup

roundup runs coding Agents in a Project and shows the user their Status, Todos, Pads, Messages and Terminals. rup is how an Agent reads and changes all of that from its shell: every command acts as you, the Agent whose id is in ROUNDUP_AGENT.

Human-readable command output names Agents by Rail name. IDs remain command arguments and machine fields in --json.

Examples:
  rup pad read notes
  rup terminal read 3 --after 120
  rup todo create "Fix login"
  rup pad write notes - < notes.md

Commands:

  terminal
    rup terminal open [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--workstream <workstream>]
        Start a login shell in a Terminal owned by a Workstream that is yours or in your Reach; `workstream` is required for Agents.
    rup terminal spawn <cwd> <cols> <rows> [--command <command>]... --env <env>
        Start a program in a Terminal owned by you; the answer holds its `id`.
    rup terminal close <id>
        Stop a Terminal you or your Reach own and forget it.
    rup terminal write <id> [<text>] [--no-enter] [--base64 <base64>]
        Type text into a Terminal you or your Reach own, then press Enter.
    rup terminal resize <id> <cols> <rows>
        Resize a Terminal you or your Reach own to `cols` by `rows`.
    rup terminal kill <id>
        Stop the program of a Terminal you or your Reach own.
    rup terminal show <id>
        Show a Terminal in your Reach to the user, who sees its owner selected. [Door only]
    rup terminal screen <id>
        Read a Terminal's screen as it is now, as plain text, with the `offset` to read from next.
    rup terminal read <id> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Read a Terminal's output you have not read yet, as plain text; `next` is the offset after it.
    rup terminal search <id> <pattern> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Search a Terminal's output for a regular expression and get the matching lines with their offsets.

  agent
    rup agent spawn <cwd> [--visibility <shown>] [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--engine <engine>] [--prompt <prompt>] [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>] [--name <name>] [--model <model>] [--scout] [--specialist <specialist>] [--extras <extras>]
        Start a child Agent in a folder of this Project.
    rup agent extras
        List the skills, plugins and MCP servers of the user's setup that `agent_spawn`'s `extras` and `agent_extras_add` accept. [Door only]
    rup agent extras-add <id> --extras <extras>
        Give a running child of yours skills, plugins or MCP servers by name. [Door only]
    rup agent stop <id>
        Stop an Agent in your Reach, never yourself.
    rup agent prompt <id> <text>
        Send a prompt to an Agent in your Reach as the user would.
    rup agent interrupt <id>
        Interrupt the turn of an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent worktree-state <id>
        Read what a Worktree holds: its changes and whether it can land.
    rup agent land <id>
        Land the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach on the Base branch.
    rup agent discard <id>
        Discard the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach and its changes.
    rup agent set-order [--captured <captured>] --order <order>
        Replace your own order: a Work order once the ask is clear, or a Clarification order while a question is open.
    rup agent set-visibility <id> <visibility>
        Choose shown or internal for a direct child. [Door only]
    rup agent instructions <id>
        Read exact instruction revisions and Attempt-bound delivery facts for yourself or an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent run [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--cwd <cwd>] --command <command>...
        Run a command in a Terminal of your own that the user can watch, in your Worktree or in `cwd`.
    rup agent resume <id> [--mode <normal>]
        Continue a saved conversation in your Reach.
    rup agent context
        Ask where you stand now: whom you report to, whom to ask, your peers, your open Todos and the Models you may start a child on.
    rup agent digest
        Ask what each of your direct children did: its Kind, its last line, its open Todos and the Pads it wrote since you were last told. [Door only]
    rup agent wake <id>... [--any]
        Ask to be woken when all, or with `any` the first, of the named Agents finish (idle, done, error or needs-you).

  rail
    rup rail tree
        Read the Rail: every Group, Workstream and Agent in tree order, with each Agent Status.
    rup rail create-workstream <name> [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>]
        Make a Workstream at the Project root or in a Group.
    rup rail move <id> <index> [--parent <parent>]
        Move a node in your Reach.
    rup rail rename <id> <name>
        Rename yourself or a node in your Reach.
    rup rail start-door <id>
        Start the Door of a Workstream you made, or of one in your Reach.
    rup rail remove <id> [--scope <this>] [--operation <operation>]
        Remove a node in your Reach, never yourself.

  project

    rup project get

    rup project open <path>

    rup project start <path> --kind <agent> --name <name> --prompt <prompt>
        Start an Agent, Workstream or Mode with a prompt in a target Project through the App.

    rup import list <period>
        Read-only: list this Project's saved and live top-level Claude Code sessions active in the period, once each, with the revision to approve.

  todo
    rup todo create <title> [--body <body>] [--blockers <blockers>]... [--owner <owner>] [--priority <low>]

        Create a shared Pad.
    rup pad read <name>
        Read one Pad.
    rup pad list
        List every Pad.
    rup pad rename <name> <new-name> <expected-incarnation>

    rup pad move <name> [--home <home>]

    rup pad redo-delete <project> <restored-operation> <operation> <expected-incarnation> <expected-revision> [--expected-home <expectedHome>]
